tools.name: activate_tab
tools.title: Activate Browser Tab
tools.description: Show a debug browser's tab in its window; the browser may bring the window to the front. CDP only: a browser with a debug port (launch_browser_with_debug).

handle.description: Browser window handle. Pass handle, window or cdpPort.

window.description: Alternative to handle: a window selector.

cdpPort.description: DevTools port; found from the window when omitted. Alone, it names the browser listening on it.

tools.name: apply_layout
tools.title: Apply Layout
tools.description: Apply a previously saved layout preset. Takes one snapshot of the open windows and gives each placement its own window, never one window to two placements, preferring the window whose title, class and executable match what save_layout recorded. success is true only if every placement was arranged (and focused, for a placement with focus); status is applied, partial or failed, and placements reports each placement in order (status applied, notFound, notApplicable or failed, with window, errorCode and error). A placement matchBy cannot match (title_only on a placement without titleContains) is notApplicable with NoMatchCriterion, and one on a monitor that does not exist fails with InvalidMonitorIndex or MonitorNotFound. A monitor saved by id that is not connected falls back to the monitor with its name, then its index (monitorFallback name or index). A maximized window is given its restore rectangle, then maximized; a minimized one that stays minimized is never shown. focus lists the outcome of each focus placement that was arranged, with the same fields as focus_window (isForeground, foregroundHandle, blockingPopup, inMenuMode, errorCode). A window of an app the user's policy denies is not arranged (TargetDeniedByPolicy). dryRun changes nothing: status dryRun, each placement wouldApply or wouldLaunch with target {x, y, width, height}, or why not.

name.description: Name of the layout preset to apply

matchBy.description: How to match saved windows to current windows: 'process_and_title' (default), 'process_only' or 'title_only' (only for placements with titleContains; save_layout records none). Any other value fails with InvalidMatchBy.

launchMissing.description: Start the program or app each placement names when its window is not found (default: false); a second call can start another instance when the launched window does not match yet. For a layout an agent wrote (save_layout placements), the user is asked once per version of it; without their yes nothing is started (LaunchNotConfirmed).

dryRun.description: Only plan: report what each placement would do, and change, focus and start nothing (default false)

placements.description: Only these placements, 0-based as get_layout lists them (default: all)

tools.name: capture_region
tools.title: Capture Screen Region
tools.description: Capture an arbitrary screen region given in screen coordinates. Only the part on the screen is captured: a region partly off the screen is cut to it (warning RegionClipped, see capturedRegion), and a region entirely off it fails with RegionOffScreen. Returns the image as image content you can see (scaled: see maxDimension), followed by JSON metadata (width, height, capturedRegion, imageToScreen, filePath, captureId). Image pixels are not screen pixels: to click a point (imageX, imageY) seen in the image, pass it to the mouse tools with this captureId (valid 10 minutes, for the last 32 captures; StaleCapture once the captured window moved or the monitors changed), or convert it yourself: screenX = imageToScreen.offsetX + imageX * imageToScreen.scaleX and screenY = imageToScreen.offsetY + imageY * imageToScreen.scaleY. scaleFactor is the monitor's DPI scale, for information only; never multiply by it.

x.description: X coordinate of the region's left edge

y.description: Y coordinate of the region's top edge

width.description: Width of the region in pixels

height.description: Height of the region in pixels

format.description: Image format: 'auto' (default: JPEG, or PNG when the image's long edge is at most 512 pixels), 'png' (lossless, larger) or 'jpeg' ('jpg' is accepted too). With outputPath, 'auto' follows the file extension. Any other value is rejected with InvalidFormat.

quality.description: JPEG quality, clamped to 1-100. Only used for JPEG. Default: 80

maxDimension.description: Longest edge of the image in pixels; larger captures are scaled down proportionally. Default (null): 1568, the size vision models work at. 0 keeps full resolution. imageToScreen reports the resulting scale.

output.description: What to return: 'image' (default: the image and the metadata), 'file' (write the image to a file and return only the metadata with filePath), 'both' (image, file and metadata) or 'metadata' (only the metadata, no image). Any other value is rejected with InvalidOutputMode.

outputPath.description: Absolute path on a drive letter (no network or device paths) of the image file for output 'file' or 'both', ending in .png, .jpg or .jpeg to match the format. The folder must exist; it is not created. Default: a new file in %TEMP%\WindowsAppManagerMcp\captures.

overwrite.description: Allow outputPath to replace an existing file. Default: false, which reports an existing file as FileExists.

saveToFile.description: Deprecated alias for output 'file': true writes the image to a file and returns only the metadata. Default: false

maxWidth.description: Deprecated: maximum image width in pixels. Given without maxDimension it replaces the 1568 default and limits only the width; with maxDimension both limits apply.

includeCursor.description: Draw the mouse pointer into the image (default: false). The result always says where it is (cursor)

gridSpacing.description: Draw a grid every this many screen pixels (20-10000), labeled with screen coordinates, to read points off the image

zoom.description: Enlarge the image 1-4 times (default 1) to read small text or controls; maxDimension still caps its long edge; an image over 64 megapixels is InvalidImageSize

tools.name: capture_window
tools.title: Capture Window
tools.description: Capture a specific window, even when other windows cover it. A minimized window fails with WindowMinimized (or pass restoreIfMinimized), a hidden one with WindowHidden, one on another virtual desktop with Cloaked, and a window of an app the user's policy denies with TargetDeniedByPolicy. A window that is not responding is captured as the compositor last showed it, or copied from the screen (warning WindowNotResponding). Returns the image as image content you can see (scaled: see maxDimension), followed by JSON metadata (width, height, capturedRegion, imageToScreen, filePath, captureId). A successful capture can carry warnings, each starting with a code: ImageBlank (one solid color), WindowNotResponding (copied from the screen, covering windows show), DpiScaledWindow, RegionClipped and others. capturedRegion and imageToScreen use the window's real screen position: the visible frame's corner, or the client area's corner when includeFrame is false. With ref, the image is cropped to that element (plus padding) for a small, sharp view of one control; the crop's corner is its origin. Image pixels are not screen pixels: to click a point (imageX, imageY) seen in the image, pass it to the mouse tools with this captureId (valid 10 minutes, for the last 32 captures; StaleCapture once the captured window moved or the monitors changed), or convert it yourself: screenX = imageToScreen.offsetX + imageX * imageToScreen.scaleX and screenY = imageToScreen.offsetY + imageY * imageToScreen.scaleY. scaleFactor is the monitor's DPI scale, for information only; never multiply by it.

handle.description: Window handle (as integer) from find_windows. Pass handle or window, not both; with ref both may be left out.

window.description: Alternative to handle: a window selector (its fields filter as find_windows' do; processName is the whole name), resolved to exactly one window or refused (AmbiguousWindow lists candidates).

ref.description: The element to crop the image to: a ref from an earlier read, such as 'w4120035e17' (its bounds are read again now), plus padding, clipped to the window. The window is the ref's own; a handle or window that names another fails with InvalidArguments. ElementStale or AmbiguousElement when the element is gone, ElementOffscreen when it is offscreen or outside the window.

padding.description: Pixels of the window kept around the ref's element on every side (0-500). Default: 8. Only with ref.

includeFrame.description: Whether to include the window frame/decoration (title bar, borders). Default: true

format.description: Image format: 'auto' (default: JPEG, or PNG when the image's long edge is at most 512 pixels), 'png' (lossless, larger) or 'jpeg' ('jpg' is accepted too). With outputPath, 'auto' follows the file extension. Any other value is rejected with InvalidFormat.

quality.description: JPEG quality, clamped to 1-100. Only used for JPEG. Default: 80

maxDimension.description: Longest edge of the image in pixels; larger captures are scaled down proportionally. Default (null): 1568, the size vision models work at. 0 keeps full resolution. imageToScreen reports the resulting scale.

output.description: What to return: 'image' (default: the image and the metadata), 'file' (write the image to a file and return only the metadata with filePath), 'both' (image, file and metadata) or 'metadata' (only the metadata, no image). Any other value is rejected with InvalidOutputMode.

outputPath.description: Absolute path on a drive letter (no network or device paths) of the image file for output 'file' or 'both', ending in .png, .jpg or .jpeg to match the format. The folder must exist; it is not created. Default: a new file in %TEMP%\WindowsAppManagerMcp\captures.

overwrite.description: Allow outputPath to replace an existing file. Default: false, which reports an existing file as FileExists.

saveToFile.description: Deprecated alias for output 'file': true writes the image to a file and returns only the metadata. Default: false

maxWidth.description: Deprecated: maximum image width in pixels. Given without maxDimension it replaces the 1568 default and limits only the width; with maxDimension both limits apply.

restoreIfMinimized.description: Restore a minimized window (or the minimized window it is inside) for the capture without activating it, wait until it has painted, capture, then minimize it again without activating another window. Default: false, which refuses a minimized window with WindowMinimized. While the window is restored the call holds the input gate, so it fails with PausedByUser while input is paused, and it is refused with TargetDeniedByPolicy when the policy denies a window the restore would show. A hidden or cloaked window is not restored. A window that was maximized before it was minimized is captured at its normal size and may restore un-maximized afterwards.

captureMethod.description: How the pixels are read: 'auto' (default: PrintWindow, falling back to the compositor), 'printwindow', 'wgc' (Windows.Graphics.Capture, for windows that print black) or 'screen' (covering windows included)

includeCursor.description: Draw the mouse pointer into the image (default: false). The result always says where it is (cursor)

gridSpacing.description: Draw a grid every this many screen pixels (20-10000), labeled with screen coordinates, to read points off the image

tools.name: capture_with_elements
tools.title: Capture Window with Element Boxes
tools.description: Capture a window with its UI elements drawn on it as numbered marks (Set-of-Marks): a box per element and a filled tag with the element's ref, such as w4120035e17; when all marks' refs share their window part, the tags leave it out (e17) and markPrefix gives it (w4120035). Act on a mark with element_action(ref) (no coordinates), or pass its legend center to mouse_click with this captureId. Returns the image as image content you can see (scaled: see maxDimension), followed by JSON metadata (width, height, capturedRegion, imageToScreen, filePath, captureId). The metadata's legend has one line per mark: '[ref] Type 'Name' #automationId center=(x,y)', center in pixels of the returned image. By default only elements with an action pattern (button, edit, check box, list item, menu item, ...) are marked, at most 80. The image is returned even when the UI Automation walk fails or times out: then elementsError and elementsErrorCode say why, and truncated is true whenever the element list is incomplete. A window is refused as in capture_window (WindowMinimized unless restoreIfMinimized, WindowHidden, Cloaked, TargetDeniedByPolicy). A successful capture can carry warnings, each starting with a code: ImageBlank (one solid color), WindowNotResponding (copied from the screen, covering windows show), DpiScaledWindow, RegionClipped and others. handle.description: Window handle (as integer) from find_windows. Pass handle or window, not both.

window.description: Alternative to handle: a window selector (its fields filter as find_windows' do; processName is the whole name), resolved to exactly one window or refused (AmbiguousWindow lists candidates).

includeFrame.description: Whether to include the window frame/decoration. Default: true

format.description: Image format: 'auto' (default: JPEG, or PNG when the image's long edge is at most 512 pixels), 'png' (lossless, larger) or 'jpeg' ('jpg' is accepted too). With outputPath, 'auto' follows the file extension. Any other value is rejected with InvalidFormat.

quality.description: JPEG quality, clamped to 1-100. Only used for JPEG. Default: 80

maxDepth.description: How many levels below the window to read (clamped to 1-10). 1 reads only the window's direct children. Default: 5

controlTypes.description: Comma-separated control types to keep (e.g., 'Button,Edit'). Leave empty for all types. Matching elements inside containers of other types are still returned: the containers are left out and their matches take their place. Unknown names fail with InvalidControlType, which lists the valid names. Common types: Button, Edit, CheckBox, ComboBox, ListItem, MenuItem, TabItem, Text, Hyperlink, Image, Pane, Group.

Labels and containers are left out, but the elements inside them are still marked. Default: true when controlTypes is empty, false with controlTypes.

labels.description: Draw each mark's ref as a filled tag at its box. Default: true. false draws the boxes only.

Default (null): 1568, the size vision models work at. 0 keeps full resolution. imageToScreen reports the resulting scale. imageBounds are scaled with the image; screenBounds stay in screen pixels.
